## funnel_metrics

Derived metrics computed from landed [`funnels`](google_analytics.qmd#funnels)
rows - currently task success rates, one per funnel.

Each row represents one metric's value, for one funnel run, for one relying
party (or the funnel's total across all relying parties).

`Keywords`: Google Analytics, GA4, funnel, task success, task success rate,
derived metric

### Provenance

Like a funnel's steps, a funnel's derived metrics are declared in that
funnel's YAML on GitHub, in a `metrics:` block - see
[`funnel_src/funnels/`](https://github.com/cds-snc/canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline/tree/main/infra/modules/google_analytics/funnel_src/funnels)
in the `canadalogin-reporting-data-pipeline` repo. **The YAML is the canonical
definition of what each metric measures**, including which two steps a ratio
divides. A separate Lambda reads the already-landed rows from
[`funnels`](google_analytics.qmd#funnels) (no new GA4 call) and computes every
metric each funnel declares. See the
[task success rate](../cookbook/google_analytics.qmd#task-success-rate)
cookbook entry for how the one metric type in use today (`step_ratio`) is
calculated and interpreted.

* **Updated**: Daily, at 06:45 ET, after the 06:30 ET funnel export
* **Steward**: EDCP Data and Research Team
* **Contact**: [Colin Douglas](mailto:colin.douglas@cds-snc.ca)
* **Location**: `s3://<transformed-bucket>/google_analytics/funnel_metrics/`

### Fields

One row per `funnel_id` per `funnel_version` per `window_days` per
`window_end` per `metric_id` per `breakdown_value`.

| Field Name | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| funnel_id | string | Partition key. Which funnel this metric was computed from (for example, "sign_in", "sign_up") |
| funnel_version | string | Partition key. The funnel definition's version the metric was computed under. Typed `string` by the crawler - see the [`funnels`](google_analytics.qmd#funnels) Notes |
| window_days | string | Partition key. Length of the reporting window: "1" (nightly monitor), "7" (rolling weekly rate), or "28" (rolling four-week rate) |
| window_end | string | Partition key. Last date (inclusive) of the reporting window, as text |
| metric_id | string | Which metric this row is. Declared per-funnel on GitHub; currently always "task_success" for both funnels, but not a closed set - see Provenance |
| metric_type | string | The metric's calculation shape, from the same YAML declaration. Currently always "step_ratio" (one step's `activeusers` over another's) |
| value | double | The computed metric value. `null`, not `0.0`, when the denominator is zero (nobody entered, so the rate is undefined - not a false zero) |
| breakdown_dimension | string | The bare dimension the source funnel's `breakdown:` block splits by (currently always "rp_name") |
| breakdown_value | string | The relying party this row covers, or `RESERVED_TOTAL` for the funnel's overall value - see [`funnels`](google_analytics.qmd#funnels) Notes |
| window_start | string | First date (inclusive) of the reporting window, as text |
| window_incomplete | boolean | `true` if the underlying funnel window was trimmed to `valid_from`/`valid_to` - **exclude these rows from a trend**, same rule as [`funnels`](google_analytics.qmd#funnels) |

### Notes

**This table deliberately does not carry the raw step values a ratio was
computed from** - only the result. The inputs are recoverable by joining back
to [`funnels`](google_analytics.qmd#funnels) on the same
`(funnel_id, funnel_version, window_days, window_end, breakdown_value)`, if
they're needed.

**Same versioning caveat as `funnels`, and the same fix applies**: always pin
`funnel_version`, or query
[`funnel_metrics_current`](google_analytics.qmd#funnel_metrics_current) rather
than this table directly.

**A metric is recomputed automatically when its funnel's `funnel_version`
bumps** (the same nightly job backfills every past window under the new
version), but adding a `metrics:` block to a funnel for the first time also
triggers a one-time backfill across that funnel's entire already-landed
history - so a metric's earliest `window_end` is not necessarily the date the
metric was defined.
